dossier.public_summary: The 0.505-day dip lines up exactly with the star's 0.504-day spin, with variability amplitudes several times larger than the dip and a strong brightness swing at the same period. The dip depth also changes five-fold between sectors and within the same pipeline, which a planet cannot do. The long duration and poor density fit further favour evolving starspots creating flat-like minima over a transiting planet.

reasons.why: Dip repeats at the stellar rotation period (1:1) in every sector with rotation amplitudes 15425 to 47365 ppm much larger than the dip. Coincident period and huge amplitude indicates rotational modulation, not a planet transit.

Depth changes by a factor of ~5 between sectors and changes within a single source (QLP p_constant 5.765797882985046e-07, SPOC p_constant 6.745943760378342e-34), inconsistent with a planet. sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source.

Very large out-of-eclipse swing at the same period (0.59x dip depth, high chi2) plus duration much longer than central transit (1.73x) and very poor stellar-density match favours spots/grazing binary over a planet. Shape appears flat (v_sigma -7.356) because spot minima are flat-bottomed.

reasons.why: Centroid is on target, ruling out a neighbour eclipse, but does not require a planet when the target's own variability reproduces the signal. No plausible neighbour within 1 pixel to cause dip.
